title: Signal Compass — Condensed Feature Requests + Triage (Aug 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

This note consolidates the top recurring customer asks we surfaced during Jul–Aug 2026 account work (mid-market + 3 enterprise pilots). Goal: provide a compact, actionable map so Product + Eng can decide quick wins vs investment projects. This is intentionally condensed — see linked artifacts for raw threads, call notes, and annotated transcripts.

How this doc is organized:
- Topline signals (what customers actually say, grouped by theme)
- Concrete feature asks (canonical phrasing customers use)
- Impact and evidence (who asked, how often, severity)
- Rough sizing and proposed owners (t-shirt + suggested team)
- Quick next steps and trial actions
- Open questions / risks / notes to self

Topline signals (high-level themes)
1) Predictable cost controls: customers want per-route/per-model token visibility and hard budget limits. Multiple accounts are surprised by burst cost patterns (surprising token counts, retries, and fallback cascades).
2) Safer rollouts & model pinning: requests for stable per-route model pins with canary percent and auto-fallback chain that is visible and auditable.
3) Latency/cost tradeoff controls: easy toggles in Console/SDK to prefer lower-cost quantized variants when tail latency tolerance is higher.
4) Caching & prompt hygiene controls: customers want finer-grained prefix caching toggles and visibility into cache hit/miss by route and user.
5) Debugging observability: token-level traces, sample-level outputs, prompt-attribution heatmaps; i.e., show which prompt segments drove hallucination/cost.
6) Enterprise onboarding friction: clearer checklist for Private deployments (KMS, network, HSMs) and guided infra templates.

Canonical customer asks (verbatim-ish paraphrases):
- “We need a per-endpoint budget cap — if exceeded, fail predictable, don’t spill into higher-cost models.” — mid-market analytics platform (3 inbound threads)
- “Can we pin a model to the route and also have an automatic fallback policy that we author?” — enterprise security customer (1 pilot, multiple calls)
- “Show token breakdown right next to the request trace so I can see why a bill spiked.” — growth-stage startup (support ticket + Slack)
- “Give us an option to prefer 4-bit quantized variant for background batch jobs.” — AI-native SaaS (customer success field note)
- “Cache hit rates per-key and per-route — we need to tune prompt templates without guessing.” — e-comm company (POC)

Evidence & signals (counts and sources):
- High-confidence: mentioned by >=3 different customers or escalated by an AE/SE in past 6 weeks: predictable cost controls, model pinning, cache visibility. (See linked Slack thread + JIRA CS-1284 notes.)
- Medium-confidence: latency/cost toggles and token-level traces — 1–2 accounts vocal, but multiple internal engineers requested the same in workshops.
- Low-confidence but strategic: onboarding templates for Private — only single enterprise pilot asked directly but aligns with GTM roadmap.

Impact estimate (customer value if shipped):
- Per-route budget caps: High value — prevents billing surprises, reduces churn risk for SMBs.
- Model pin + fallback UI: High value for enterprise customers (reduces rollback friction, compliance traceability).
- Token breakdown in Console: Medium-high: reduces time-to-diagnose but requires backend instrumentation work.
- Caching controls + visibility: Medium: saves token cost for workloads with repeated prefixes, revenue enablement for heavy-chat customers.

Rough sizing & suggested owners (quick t-shirt, dev intensity and suggested team)
1) Per-route budget caps (M) — Product: hosted-api; Eng: platform-engineering + billing. Related Jira: JIRA:CS-1284. Suggested owner: Product (Jordan Lee) + Eng (Billing infra).
2) Model pinning + configurable fallback policy (L→M) — Product: console-and-rollouts; Eng: serving-runtime + routing. Owner: Rollouts PM (Priya Nair).
3) Token-level cost breakdown in Console (M) — Product: console; Eng: observability + cost-aggregation pipeline. Owner: Observability lead (Tom Alvarez).
4) Cache hit/miss per-route (S) — Product: optimize; Eng: serving-runtime. Owner: Optimize PM (Sophie Chen).
5) Console toggle to prefer quantized variants for a route (L) — Product: optimize; Eng: compilation & runtime. Owner: Applied ML eng lead.

Quick wins (0–6 weeks)
- Surface “estimated token cost” in API response headers for hosted customers (engineering + API docs change). Low risk, immediate value. Suggest ship as feature-flag behind billing-visibility. Linked: PR #87.
- Add a “fail on budget-exceed” flag per API key/route that returns 402 and logs the event. Minimal UI required; can be rolled out via SDK flag. (Short-lived experiment.)
- Exportable CSV of recent requests with token counts and sequence length distributions for customer support to triage bills faster.

Medium-term (6–14 weeks)
- Model pin + fallback UI + audit trail. Requires routing changes and Console UX. Coordinate with SRE for rollout tests.
- Cache telemetry (per-route hit/miss). Start with a sampling mode to limit telemetry volume.

Longer-term (Q4+)
- Built-in quantized recommendations engine in Optimize that suggests per-route profiles. Integrate with rollout automation.
- Guided Private onboarding templates (network/KMS/HSM) + terraform module for common partner clouds.

Open questions & risks
- Billing semantics: how do budget caps interplay with reserved/dedicated committed usage? Need Finance input. (Flag: @Finance ops)
- Data retention for token-level traces: privacy and storage cost tradeoffs. Legal + Security check required for PII redaction.
- Fallback safety: automatic fallback to cheaper model could change output quality; require evals + automatic regression detection.

Notes to self / field tips (informal):
- When triaging billing spikes, ask customers for: representative request ID, timestamp (UTC), model name, route name, and a raw prompt snippet. Saves a lot of back-and-forth.
- Internal shorthand used during calls: “pin+chain” = route-level model pin with fallback chain; define this in Product glossary to reduce ambiguity.

Proposed immediate action items (owners & dates):
- A) Ship API response header for estimated tokens (Eng: API infra) — owner: Tom A. — target: 2026-09-01 (MVP)
- B) Experiment: SDK flag to fail-on-budget (Product & CS) — owner: Jordan L. — target: 2026-08-30
- C) Prototype cache-hit exporter (S) — owner: Sophie C. — target: 2026-09-15 (sampling only)

Appendix: selective raw customer quotes (redacted org names)
- “Our month-end bill spiked 3x — there was no clear way to see which requests caused it.” — customer A (support ticket 2026-07-21)
- “If we could pin a model per route and see an audit trail, compliance would be much easier.” — customer B (pilot kickoff)
- “A console toggle to prefer cheaper variants for background tasks would save us thousands.” — customer C (post-call note)

Raw artifacts & where to find them:
- Full annotated call transcripts: confluence link above
- Slack thread w/ AE flags: https://slack-redwood/archives/CUST-voice/p1673401200
- Related PR for header change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbook/pull/87

If you want a 1-pager for Exec or a deck for AMs, I can produce a slide summary with the quick-wins highlighted.

-- Sophie (notes from CS sync 2026-08-12 -> 08-14)

Unresolved: confirm Finance semantics on per-route budget caps vs Dedicated reserved capacity billing. Follow-up: assign to Finance liaison and schedule 30-min sync before Aug 25.
